clauses.reason: The first scope is the order’s recitals and section 1, signed 1961-01-24. Section 1 amends Executive Order 10900 (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954) by renumbering sections 6 and 7 and inserting a new section 6 under which the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program "shall be responsible for" the continuous supervision and coordination of the functions delegated or assigned to officers or agencies of the Government. The recitals are not operative commands. Later event: Executive Order 11252, signed 1965-10-20 and taking effect 1965-11-01, transfers all functions of the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program, including those under EO 10900 as amended, to the Secretary of State and says that order is modified accordingly, without restating section 6. It does not name EO 10915 or section 6 and prints no replacement text, so what remained of section 6 afterwards is not shown by held text; I record it as a later event and disclose it as an earlier candidate end that held evidence does not establish (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments). Other later orders that amend EO 10900 (EO 10972, EO 11036, EO 11963, EO 12148) concern other sections: section 4 paragraphs, section 4(a), a new subsection of section 1, and section 4(d)(2), and the dossier’s missing lines for EO 11963, EO 12148 and EO 12220 are resolved by reading those texts. First end: Executive Order 12220, signed 1980-06-27, revokes EO 10900 as amended; the cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 12220 (the dossier’s actor context), whose section 1-501 says "Executive Order N o. 10900 o f January 5,1961, as am ended, is revoked." EO 12220 has no effective-date wording of its own, so the signing date is recorded; the Federal Register publication date 1980-07-01 is the alternative reading. Section 6 of EO 10900 therefore ended with that revocation.

Section 2 of Executive Order 10915 is the command to amend Executive Order 10893 (administration of mutual security and related functions) by adding a new section 111 at the end of Part I. First end: Executive Order 10973, signed 1961-11-03, supersedes it by name: section 605 ("Superseded orders.") lists, as item (b), "Section 2 of Executive Order No." 10915 (26 F.R. 781), and as item (a) EO 10893 except Part II. Its section 607 makes the order’s provisions "shall become effective" as of September 30, 1961, so the end date recorded is 1961-09-30, the stated effective date; the signing date 1961-11-03 and the filing date 1961-11-06 are the alternative readings, and a retroactive date is disclosed for the reviewer. The cited source is the whole held Federal Register text of EO 10973 (the dossier’s actor context), because the dossier’s located-provision records for this pair are American Presidency Project transcriptions that would need a separate page check.

The text of new section 111 of Executive Order 10893, as inserted by section 2 of EO 10915, makes the Director of the Food-for-Peace Program responsible, subject to the direction of the President, for supervision and coordination of the functions under section 402 of the Act, without superseding any other delegation. It has the same end as section 2: Executive Order 10973 supersedes section 2 of EO 10915 by name (section 605, item (b)) and supersedes EO 10893 except Part II (item (a)); section 111 sits in Part I, which section 111 itself was added to. Recorded end: 1961-09-30, the effective date stated in section 607 of EO 10973 ("shall become effective"), with the signing date 1961-11-03 as the alternative reading.

research_rationale:
EO 10915 amends EO 10900 (new section 6, Director of the Food-for-Peace Program) and EO 10893 (new section 111); provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed the dossier’s three-scope inventory (recitals and section 1; section 2; the inserted section 111). Section 2 and section 111 end on 1961-09-30 by EO 10973 section 605 and 607. Section 1 ends on 1980-06-27 by EO 12220 section 1-501, which revokes EO 10900; the 1965 transfer of the Director’s functions (EO 11252) is a later event and an undetermined earlier candidate. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1980-06-27.

savings.reason: Section 606 of EO 10973 ("Saving provisions.") continues determinations, regulations, orders and other actions made with respect to any function affected by that order and not revoked or made inapplicable before its date, until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority; actions taken under section 111 or section 6 are accrued effects and the functions they concerned were reassigned by EO 10973, EO 11252 and EO 12220. These accrued actions do not keep sections 6 or 111 operative. EO 12220 has no saving clause of its own.
